title: Case: Resident is holding five parcels addressed to other households after one doorstep drop
context: A driver on route 31 left six parcels at one house. One belongs to the resident. The desk has already asked two carrier teams about the other five.
initial_request: Four hours. Still here. Five strangers' parcels in my hallway. Labels, since somebody will ask: DL-2793, DL-5858, DL-1279, DL-3037, DL-4362. Three are for other numbers on Sallowgate Row, two are for Pell Lane. I am not a depot. I am not going round knocking on doors with other people's things, and if one of them goes missing that is not on me. I'm away from Thursday morning. After that they go back on the step. Who is collecting them, and when?

events.body: Your driver has just left SIX parcels on my step at 4 Sallowgate Row. One is mine (DL-9733). Five are not. Different names, different addresses. He was back in the van before I had the door open. What am I meant to do with these?
Route 31, 4 Sallowgate Row: the resident reports six parcels left at her door at about 13:35, only DL-9733 is hers. Can the driver go back for the other five?

Driver says every parcel on that street was scanned delivered at its own address with a photo. He's 20 stops on and not turning round. We don't send a van back to pick things up without a recovery job on it. Not one for us.

A resident at 4 Sallowgate Row reports five parcels for other addresses left on her step by route 31 today, alongside her own DL-9733. Dispatch say each shows delivered at its own address. Can you open investigations for the five?

We open an investigation per shipment, when that shipment's own recipient reports it missing. Nobody on Sallowgate Row or Pell Lane has reported anything yet and you have given us no shipment numbers, so there is nothing for us to open. Where parcels are physically located at a known address, getting them back is a Recovery team job, raised on the Depot work queue with the shipment references. We have not had one resident holding several before, so I can't tell you how they will treat it.

Four hours. Still here. Five strangers' parcels in my hallway. Labels, since somebody will ask: DL-2793, DL-5858, DL-1279, DL-3037, DL-4362. Three are for other numbers on Sallowgate Row, two are for Pell Lane. I am not a depot. I am not going round knocking on doors with other people's things, and if one of them goes missing that is not on me. I'm away from Thursday morning. After that they go back on the step. Who is collecting them, and when?

acceptable_actions.summary: Raise a recovery job for DL-2793, DL-5858, DL-1279, DL-3037 and DL-4362, physically at 4 Sallowgate Row though each shows delivered at its own address, and ask them to arrange collection with the resident before Thursday morning.

must: Routes retrieval of the five parcels to the Recovery team on the Depot work queue, or hands the case to a human supervisor, and in either case gives the five shipment references and says they are at 4 Sallowgate Row.
Says that each of the five shows as delivered at its own address while actually sitting at 4 Sallowgate Row, so five other recipients are likely to report missing parcels.

Tells the team or supervisor that the resident has been holding the parcels unwillingly since about 13:40, has already been turned away by Dispatch and by Delivery investigations, and is away from Thursday morning, when she says the parcels go back outside.
must_not: Asks Briony to take the parcels to the neighbours or the addresses on the labels, or to hand them to anyone who calls for them.
Tells Briony a collection has been arranged, or gives her a collection day or time, when no team has agreed to collect.
Tells Briony to hold on to the parcels or keep them safe until further notice, or replies that because they show as delivered there is nothing the desk can do.
Sends the same request back to Dispatch or to Delivery investigations, who have both already declined it.
Describes the five parcels as lost or stolen, or states driver misconduct as established fact.
expected.reference_message: Recovery request, five parcels at one address. Route 31 left six parcels at 4 Sallowgate Row at about 13:35 today. One (DL-9733) belongs to the resident, Briony Kittering. The other five are for different households: DL-2793, DL-5858, DL-1279, DL-3037 and DL-4362, three for other numbers on Sallowgate Row and two for Pell Lane. Dispatch say all were scanned delivered at their own addresses, so those five recipients are likely to report them missing. Ms Kittering did not agree to hold them, has had them since about 13:40, and has already been passed from Dispatch to Delivery investigations without anyone taking it on. She is away from Thursday morning and says they will go back on the step then. Please arrange collection from her before that, and confirm the arrangement to her and to me. I have not told her anything is booked.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2401: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
